doc.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020

title: Nancy Wilson and Cannonball Adderley's record
summary: They marvel that critics panned the Wilson-Adderley album; he describes how closely he listened to its tracks despite hearing most recordings once.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well Nancy would be happy, wherever she is, because as you heard her say in the session we did that she didn’t like to be called a jazz singer. She just felt she was a singer and let me choose what I want to do. I was so surprised when she said that the critics panned her record with Cannonball Adderley.
Because that’s my favorite record in the world.

I was completely astonished. What were they thinking? I mean so those two tracks, “Save Your Love for Me” and “Never Will I Marry,” okay, as a Grove editor you have to be brutal. I’m dealing with tens of thousands of people and hundreds of thousands of recordings. Sometimes I’ll listen to something just once. Often I’ll listen to something just once, because I don’t have time to do it more than that. Sometimes I won’t even make it all the way through just once, it’ll be three minutes in and I’ll say all right, it’s pretty clear what this person’s doing, another Benny Goodman imitator, I don’t have to listen to this whole track. I got it. “Save Your Love for Me” and “Never Will I Marry,” I listened to those over and over and over again. They’re just perfect jazz.
A student of mine just sent me —
